title: Becoming the drummer on the Old Kentucky Minstrels
summary: When the drummer fell ill he played parade and show, was offered the job at six dollars, and describes life on the car.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: I see. What did you do with the Old Kentucky Minstrels? Pretty much the same thing you were doing before?

About the same thing. But I got the (?)... Before I left... I think before I left the Old Kentucky Minstrels, I was able to play drums in the parade. That's when the drummer taken sick, and they asked could I play...could I play the parade and the show? Well, I had confidence in myself. I told them, yes, I could play the parade and the show. I didn't know if I could or not, but I mean... But the drummer taken sick, and I played the parade, go on downtown, played on the corner, and played coming back. Meanwhile(?) I hung up the coats for them to dry out in time for the show. The show started at seven o'clock. I had my drums all set up, some old broke-down drums, a big old 28-inch bass drum, old broke-down pedal. I played the show.

Did that about two nights. And the man... I was a bit younger, and other drummer had taken sick. So the owner(?) called ...(??)...(??)...., and asked did I want the job steady. I said, "What about the other drummer?" He said, "Well, he's sick, and we're going to get rid of him. We want you." I said, "No, don't get rid of him. He did the show a long time." He said, "Well, if you don't take the

job, I have to get somebody else."
So they decided to give me six dollars...a night. Six dollars a night or a week...? I can't remember... I think it was a week. Get the meals, sleep on the car... During that time I didn't have no laundry, but we had shift/slip(?) shirts. You'd wash them out after the set and hang them up, and they would dry in about ten minutes. We all had to wear the same thing.
